questions.question: Describe the key types of non-verbal communication and explain how each conveys meaning.

points.text: Types of NVC: body language (posture and gestures convey openness or defensiveness), facial expressions (convey six basic emotions universally), eye contact (signals interest or threat), proxemics (personal space zones signal relationship closeness), paralinguistics (tone and pitch convey emotion beyond words). Each type provides additional information beyond spoken language.

questions.question: Evaluate whether facial expressions are universal or culturally specific, using research evidence.

points.text: Ekman found universal recognition of six basic emotions across cultures, including the Fore tribe in Papua New Guinea who had limited Western contact. This supports the nature view (innate expressions). However, display rules vary: Japanese participants masked negative emotions more than Americans (Ekman & Friesen). Conclusion: facial expressions are biologically based but culturally regulated.

questions.question: Explain how proxemics can affect social interactions, referring to Hall's zones of personal space.

points.text: Hall's four zones: intimate (close family/partners), personal (friends), social (colleagues/acquaintances), public (strangers/speeches). Being too close causes discomfort and anxiety (e.g. crowded lifts). Violating personal space can be used deliberately to intimidate or show intimacy. Cultural differences exist: some cultures prefer more personal space than others.
